text.en:
Sei lì. — You are there.
Sei lì? — Are you there?
The words are the same.
Only the question mark changes.
When you say it, your voice goes up at the end.

Paolo è in ufficio? — Is Paolo at the office?
Lea è alla stazione? — Is Lea at the train station?
Alla stazione means “at the station”.
English swaps the words: “Is Paolo…”.
Italian keeps the order and adds the question mark.

Sei pronto? — Are you ready?
Lei è pronta? — Is she ready?
Next, you build each question from word pieces.
Pick the words as for a normal sentence.
The question mark is added for you.
